classification.difficultyReason: Find where each function crosses the y-axis, then evaluate separate definite integrals for regions on either side.

content.prompt: In each part, find the area of the region bounded by the function and the $y$-axis between the specified values. Areas to the right and to the left of the $y$-axis must be calculated separately.

answer.worked:
$x=y-5$ is zero at $y=5$. For $0\le y<5$, $x<0$ (left of the $y$-axis). For $5<y\le6$, $x>0$ (right of the $y$-axis).

Left:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{left}}&=-\int_0^5(y-5)\,dy\\&=-\left[\frac{y^2}{2}-5y\right]_0^5\\&=-\left(\frac{25}{2}-25\right)\\&=\frac{25}{2}\end{align*}$$
Right:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{right}}&=\int_5^6(y-5)\,dy\\&=\left[\frac{y^2}{2}-5y\right]_5^6\\&=(18-30)-\left(\frac{25}{2}-25\right)\\&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{total}}&=\frac{25}{2}+\frac12\\&=13\text{ u}^2\end{align*}$$

$x=3-y$ is zero at $y=3$. For $2\le y<3$, $x>0$ (right of the $y$-axis). For $3<y\le5$, $x<0$ (left of the $y$-axis).

Right:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{right}}&=\int_2^3(3-y)\,dy\\&=\left[3y-\frac{y^2}{2}\right]_2^3\\&=\left(9-\frac92\right)-(6-2)\\&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Left:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{left}}&=-\int_3^5(3-y)\,dy\\&=-\left[3y-\frac{y^2}{2}\right]_3^5\\&=-\left[\left(15-\frac{25}{2}\right)-\left(9-\frac92\right)\right]\\&=2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{total}}&=\frac12+2\\&=\frac52\\&=2\frac12\text{ u}^2\end{align*}$$
